label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, provider-outage, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Its diagnosis named no action, so nobody was asked to approve one. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing: this fault's cause is not a deploy.

fault.name: provider-outage
fault.title: Payments fail: the provider hangs, and our circuit breaker fails fast
fault.cause: the provider's charge and refund API hangs (5 s, then 503): our payments API's calls to it time out, each after 3 attempts, until its circuit breaker opens, after 5 calls in a row got no answer; from then on it fails fast, answering 503 'outcome unknown' at once without calling the provider, and lets one trial call through 10 s after it opened, and again after each trial that fails
expected_symptoms: clients get 503 'outcome unknown', most of them at once: the 5xx share of POST /payments climbs

the first calls still wait out their 3 timed-out attempts (about 10 s) until the breaker opens; after that only the trial calls wait, the first 10 s after it opened, then one 10 s after each that fails: the p95 latency may climb for about a minute, then drops
provider calls end with no answer (timeouts) at first, klaxon.provider.attempts result no_answer; then the breaker refuses them, klaxon.provider.refused
the payments API logs 'circuit breaker open', and its health check keeps passing: once the breaker opens, its worker threads are free again
the money check passes: nothing was charged, so no money is wrong

after it ends, the next trial call gets an answer and the breaker closes; payments and refunds whose outcome stayed unknown stay pending, with nothing charged or refunded: they need a decision (retry them with their keys, or mark them failed), and until then such a refund blocks new refunds on its payment
fault.remedy: nothing to change on our side: the provider must recover (escalate to it). Meanwhile the circuit breaker keeps the API answering at once, and closes again when a trial call gets an answer. After it recovers, the payments and refunds left pending need a decision (retry them with their keys, or mark them failed): a refund left pending blocks new refunds on its payment until it settles

alert.name: PaymentsErrorsHigh
alert.summary: Payments are failing: over the last minute, 92% of the answers to POST /payments on payments-api were 5xx (8.78 per second), above the threshold of 20%. Payments are slow: over the last minute, the p95 latency of POST /payments on payments-api was 4.3 s, above the threshold of 2 s.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At about 03:13:30 the provider (fake-provider, external) degraded. Some POST /v1/payments calls hung until our 3 s read timeout and a few returned 500. payments-api retries each call, so one request took 9.6 s (3 attempts of 3 s each), which pushed p95 above 2 s. The failures opened payments-api's circuit breaker. Since 03:13:56 most POST /payments requests fail fast with 503 and the payment is left pending, which gives the 92% 5xx rate. No change on our side lines up with the onset: every container was created together at 03:12:03. The breaker is shedding load as designed; it is not the cause. Open: the client metrics (c4, c5) seem not to record timeouts, so I cannot count them. I saw no provider-side data. The money check was not run, so payments the provider charged after we timed out are unverified.

evidence.shows: POST /payments 503s rise from about 0.06/s to 9.5/s from 03:13:56, while 201s drop to 0.
All services were created together at 03:12:03 with normal settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on). No deploy lines up with the onset.
payments-api errors: /v1/payments was not sent because the circuit breaker is open, and the payment was left pending.
About 6% of provider calls return 500. The call rate falls to 0 as the breaker opens, and timeouts do not appear in this metric.
A 9.6 s POST /payments (pmt_000243) made three provider calls. Each ended in an httpx ReadTimeout after about 3 s, and the request returned 503.
Provider attempts climb to about 4.3/s by 03:14:04 as retries pile up, then fall to about 0.08/s as the breaker blocks calls.
Provider calls that complete are fast (p95 about 5 ms). The latency comes from hung calls that time out.

proposed_fix.summary: No rollback is needed. Escalate the timeouts and 500s on /v1/payments to the provider, and keep the breaker on. After the provider recovers, run the money check and reconcile the pending payments, including timed-out calls the provider may have charged. Follow-up: record timeouts in the client-duration and provider-attempts metrics.

diagnosis.blast_radius: None of our services changes. Payments keep returning 503 and staying pending until the provider recovers. The provider may have charged some timed-out payments while our caller got no 201. Webhooks and the money check should resolve them.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo: this proposes no action. If the provider turns out to be healthy, reopen the investigation into payments-api's network path and its timeout settings.
